request.spec:
A person with a hold in force on the sheet's today (a hold whose dates include today) gets no cut
from any pool, and their share is spread over the other members with a cut in proportion to those
members' shares: each member's cut is the pot times their share divided by the shares of the members
with a cut, added up, rounded half to even, with the remainder to the largest share as before (when
no member is left with a cut, each shows 0.00). The pool's total share and balance are unchanged by
the hold.

A person with a hold in force on the sheet's today (a hold whose dates include today) gets no cut

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit

data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
A person on hold on the sheet's today now gets no cut from any pool, and their share is spread over the other members. All 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The whole change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/pool/Pools.java`, on the server. The person and sheet cut totals on screen are added up from the pool data, so they pick up the new cuts without any front-end change. Nothing new is stored, and no audit records change.

- **Who is on hold:** when listing pools, the server now finds everyone with a hold that includes the sheet's today (a hold with no end date counts until it is lifted).
- **New cut rule:** each member's cut is the pot × their share ÷ the total share of the members still getting a cut, rounded half to even. Members on hold or retired get 0.00. Pools that are members of another pool always get a cut.
- **Remainder:** it goes to the largest share among the members still getting a cut, the earliest added on a tie, as before.
- **Nobody left:** if no member is still getting a cut, every member shows 0.00.
- **Unchanged:** the pool's total share and whether it balances don't change.

With no holds, the new rule gives the same results as the old one: the shares of members getting a cut then add up to 100, which was the old divisor.
